question: Do the security-lab tools or the guide's machine-client example expose passwords, client secrets, bearer tokens, session cookies, or authorization codes in process arguments or environments on the host?
method: While verify-failures, verify-authentication (full), verify-log-hygiene, and the guide's machine-client example ran, a sampler read every WSL process's command line and environment as fast as possible. It counted samples containing any lab source secret (exact value) or a credential shape (JWT header prefix, 'Authorization: Bearer', session-cookie assignment, gateway callback URL, Keycloak session_code), using pattern files. Values were never printed or recorded. Controls: synthetic values placed in one process's arguments, another's environment, and a credential-shaped argument.
limitations: Sampling can miss very short-lived processes; samples_with_curl_reading_config_from_stdin shows how often curl processes were observed. Processes inside containers (the in-network probe) run in Docker's VM and are not sampled; the probe receives the session cookie on standard input. The host runs one user; other users' processes were not present.
